newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BRL Hardy to build A$18 mln winery.
newsitem.headline: BRL Hardy to build A$18 mln winery.

text.p: Australian wine producer BRL Hardy Ltd said on Thursday it would build a new A$18 million winery with a 10,000 tonne vintage capacity in the Padthaway premium grape growing region in South Australia.

BRL managing director Stephen Millar said in a statement accelerating demand for the company's premium bottled wines, particularly in the United States and United Kingdom, had fuelled the decision to expand production capacity.
"To meet this strong international and domestic growth, BRL Hardy expects to be crushing approximately 200,000 tonnes of grapes by the year 2000 compared to 157,900 for the 1996 vintage," he said.

Millar said the Padthaway winery, expected to be completed by the 1998 vintage, and the company's vineyard expansion in South Australia's southeast further entrenched the company's push to control the majority of its premium fruit supply by 2000.
BRL had spent A$50 million acquiring and expanding vineyards through Australia in the past three years, he said.
